Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Staging muster

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The front door and staging roster now share an authored, centered steel scene. After admission it shows four stable player slots with names, fixed idle-frame skin previews, gun/ability choices and waiting/ready/in-yard lamps. Existing yard players are dimmed for a late joiner; Ready becomes Drop In. Observers can watch the roster without player controls. The original previews use frame zero rather than advancing animation, and this port now follows that behavior.

All four pickers work in both directions, include automatic choices, and skip absent catalog rows. Local choices appear immediately; remote rows reflect confirmed profiles. Changing a pick clears local readiness and retires obsolete readiness retries before sending the new profile. Rapid Ready toggles use the latest local choice instead of an older authority snapshot. Restored epochs, new connections and replaced player generations reset these optimistic choices from the confirmed profile, so Ready after recovery cannot toggle an obsolete local flag. The authority still validates every profile and action.

Only the staging leader can Start, and every other connected player must already be ready. Start can ready the leader first, then waits for confirmed all-ready state before submitting Start. It cancels that intent if eligibility changes. The simulation's existing all-ready requirement is unchanged. Pick controls cannot change an already-entered player, and no world/action/event/checkpoint schema or additional gameplay-content compatibility change is needed.

The scene scrolls at smaller window heights. Existing party invite/enrollment, profile persistence and spray controls remain on the same paths beneath the new UI/Lobby/Scroll/Layout container.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/muster_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_MUSTER_CAPTURE=/absolute/output/muster.png \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/muster_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/muster_peers_run.sh

The browser UI gate now uses real staging buttons to test remote picks/unready, both cycle directions, host Start and late Drop In before running its existing gameplay/UI checks. Evidence records the actual acceptance results. Broader actor/ability presentation, original transport/death scoreboard columns, wider platform coverage and full comparison remain requirements.
